record_scope_reconstruction: Laffa/Al Laffa road crossing opposite Talatasher on the Sudan–Eritrea frontier, for the reported November 2023 suspension of Sudanese entry into Eritrea.

source_checks.finding: Original article names Laffa and Eritrea’s suspension of Sudanese entry owing to overcrowding. Its separate Gallabat–Ethiopia goods restriction is not assigned to this crossing.

UNHCR indexed article describes departure formalities at Laffa and transfer at the Eritrean checkpoint in 2004. The full-page attempt returned HTTP 429; the indexed passage verifies paired crossing identity, not the 2023 restriction.
Preserved IRIN report explicitly identifies Laffa on the Sudanese side and Talatasher on the Eritrean side of the return corridor.

sites.name: Laffa / Talatasher crossing
sites.coordinate_method: Original OSM node coordinate from independently fetched API JSON
sites.precision: approximate crossing facility area; no survey accuracy claimed
sites.evidence_note: Original extract shows control nodes between named Al-Laffa and Talatasher settlements on the Al Lafa Road corridor and the Eritrea–Sudan boundary. UNHCR independently identifies the Laffa departure formalities and Eritrean transfer checkpoint. This is distinct from Aligider/Tesseney town markers. Inspected OSM tags: {"barrier": "border_control"}. Geographic evidence only; no historical restriction or current operational status inferred.

phase_decisions.phase_applicability: Laffa/Al Laffa road crossing opposite Talatasher on the Sudan–Eritrea frontier, for the reported November 2023 suspension of Sudanese entry into Eritrea. Current phase only: Reported Eritrean suspension of Sudanese entry at Laffa

date_scope_check.qualification_retained: Observation date only. Neither initial enforcement nor lifting recovered. Gallabat’s Sunday onset is not borrowed, and the two Dabanga language versions are not independent origins. No all-traffic or continuous-duration inference. R37 endpoint check: December 2023 trade-opening preparations are prospective, the September Sudan-side reopening order predates this episode, and later movements into Sudan run in the opposite direction. None establishes restored Sudanese admission to Eritrea.
date_scope_check.review_limit: No dates, unknown reopenings, duration classifications or continuity assumptions changed by this geographic review.

unresolved: The marker locates the paired road-control area; the precise Eritrean immigration desk responsible for the 2023 decision is not identified. Aligider/Tesseney town markers are not substituted.
